passages.text: The Levitical priests—indeed the whole tribe of Levi—shall have no portion or inheritance with Israel. They are to eat the offerings made by fire to the LORD; that is their inheritance.
passages.sermon:
The Levitical priests are from the tribe of Levi.
The whole tribe of Levi is included.
They will not have a portion with Israel.
They will not have an inheritance with Israel.
They will eat the offerings made by fire to the LORD.
These offerings are their inheritance.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ יִ֠הְיֶה לַכֹּהֲנִ֨ים הַלְוִיִּ֜ם כָּל־ שֵׁ֧בֶט לֵוִ֛י חֵ֥לֶק וְנַחֲלָ֖ה עִם־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אִשֵּׁ֧י יְהוָ֛ה וְנַחֲלָת֖וֹ יֹאכֵלֽוּן׃

passages.text: Although they have no inheritance among their brothers, the LORD is their inheritance, as He promised them.
passages.sermon: The tribe of Levi has no inheritance among their brothers.\r\nThe LORD is their inheritance.\r\nThe LORD promised this to them.
passages.original: וְנַחֲלָ֥ה לֹא־ יִֽהְיֶה־ לּ֖וֹ בְּקֶ֣רֶב אֶחָ֑יו יְהוָה֙ ה֣וּא נַחֲלָת֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּר־ לֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: This shall be the priests’ share from the people who offer a sacrifice, whether a bull or a sheep: the priests are to be given the shoulder, the jowls, and the stomach.
passages.sermon:
The priests are Levites.
The priests serve God.
The people of Israel bring sacrifices to God.
The people may offer a bull or a sheep as a sacrifice.
The priests receive a share from these sacrifices.
The people must give the priest the shoulder of the animal.
The people must give the priest the jowls of the animal.
The people must give the priest the stomach of the animal.
This is the portion for the priests from the sacrifices.
passages.original: וְזֶ֡ה יִהְיֶה֩ מִשְׁפַּ֨ט הַכֹּהֲנִ֜ים מֵאֵ֣ת הָעָ֗ם מֵאֵ֛ת זֹבְחֵ֥י הַזֶּ֖בַח אִם־ שׁ֣וֹר אִם־ שֶׂ֑ה וְנָתַן֙ לַכֹּהֵ֔ן הַזְּרֹ֥עַ וְהַלְּחָיַ֖יִם וְהַקֵּבָֽה׃

passages.text: You are to give them the firstfruits of your grain, new wine, and oil, and the first wool sheared from your flock.
passages.sermon:
God chose the tribe of Levi and their sons to serve Him forever.
The Levites do not receive land as an inheritance among the other Israelites.
The LORD Himself is their inheritance.
God commanded the people to support the Levites.
You must give the Levites the firstfruits of your grain.
You must give them the first of your new wine.
You must give them the first of your oil.
You must also give them the first wool you shear from your flock.
passages.original: רֵאשִׁ֨ית דְּגָֽנְךָ֜ תִּֽירֹשְׁךָ֣ וְיִצְהָרֶ֗ךָ וְרֵאשִׁ֛ית גֵּ֥ז צֹאנְךָ֖ תִּתֶּן־ לּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: For the LORD your God has chosen Levi and his sons out of all your tribes to stand and minister in His name for all time.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
The LORD chose Levi and his sons.
The LORD chose them from all your tribes.
Levi and his sons stand before the LORD.
Levi and his sons serve in the name of the LORD.
They do this for all time.
passages.original: כִּ֣י ב֗וֹ בָּחַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ מִכָּל־ שְׁבָטֶ֑יךָ לַעֲמֹ֨ד לְשָׁרֵ֧ת בְּשֵׁם־ יְהוָ֛ה ה֥וּא וּבָנָ֖יו כָּל־ הַיָּמִֽים׃ס

passages.text: Now if a Levite moves from any town of residence throughout Israel and comes in all earnestness to the place the LORD will choose, then he shall serve in the name of the LORD his God like all his fellow Levites who stand there before the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The Levites are a tribe chosen by the LORD your God from all the tribes of Israel.
A Levite may live in any town in Israel.
If a Levite leaves his town and comes with all his desire to the place the LORD will choose,
he may come to that place freely.
He will serve in the name of the LORD his God.
He will serve just as all his fellow Levites do.
These Levites stand there before the LORD.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יָבֹ֨א הַלֵּוִ֜י מֵאַחַ֤ד שְׁעָרֶ֙יךָ֙ מִכָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁר־ ה֖וּא גָּ֣ר שָׁ֑ם וּבָא֙ בְּכָל־ אַוַּ֣ת נַפְשׁ֔וֹ אֶל־ הַמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁר־ יִבְחַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ וְשֵׁרֵ֕ת בְּשֵׁ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑יו כְּכָל־ אֶחָיו֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם הָעֹמְדִ֥ים שָׁ֖ם לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: They shall eat equal portions, even though he has received money from the sale of his father’s estate.
passages.sermon:
The Levites are the tribe chosen by the LORD your God to serve Him.
All Levites who serve at the place the LORD chooses will eat equal portions.
Each Levite will receive the same share of food as the others.
This rule applies even if a Levite has already received money from selling his father’s property.
passages.original: חֵ֥לֶק כְּחֵ֖לֶק יֹאכֵ֑לוּ לְבַ֥ד מִמְכָּרָ֖יו עַל־ הָאָבֽוֹת׃ס

passages.text: When you enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you, do not imitate the detestable ways of the nations there.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
He is giving you a land.
You will enter this land.
Do not copy the ways of the nations there.
Their ways are detestable.
Do not learn to do what they do.
passages.original: כִּ֤י אַתָּה֙ בָּ֣א אֶל־ הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נֹתֵ֣ן לָ֑ךְ לֹֽא־ תִלְמַ֣ד לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת כְּתוֹעֲבֹ֖ת הַגּוֹיִ֥ם הָהֵֽם׃

passages.text: Let no one be found among you who sacrifices his son or daughter in the fire, practices divination or conjury, interprets omens, practices sorcery, casts spells, consults a medium or spiritist, or inquires of the dead.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God gives them laws for living in the land He gives them.
God commands them not to imitate the evil practices of other nations.
No one among you must sacrifice his son in the fire.
No one among you must sacrifice his daughter in the fire.
No one among you must practice divination.
No one among you must practice conjury.
No one among you must interpret omens.
No one among you must practice sorcery.
No one among you must cast spells.
No one among you must consult a medium.
No one among you must consult a spiritist.
No one among you must inquire of the dead.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ יִמָּצֵ֣א בְךָ֔ מַעֲבִ֥יר בְּנֽוֹ־ וּבִתּ֖וֹ בָּאֵ֑שׁ קֹסֵ֣ם קְסָמִ֔ים מְעוֹנֵ֥ן וּמְנַחֵ֖שׁ וּמְכַשֵּֽׁף׃ וְחֹבֵ֖ר חָ֑בֶר וְשֹׁאֵ֥ל אוֹב֙ וְיִדְּעֹנִ֔י וְדֹרֵ֖שׁ אֶל־ הַמֵּתִֽים׃

passages.text: For whoever does these things is detestable to the LORD. And because of these detestable things, the LORD your God is driving out the nations before you.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
Anyone who does these things is detestable to the LORD.
These things are detestable practices of the nations in the land.
Because of these detestable things, the LORD your God is driving out those nations before you.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ תוֹעֲבַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה כָּל־ עֹ֣שֵׂה אֵ֑לֶּה וּבִגְלַל֙ הַתּוֹעֵבֹ֣ת הָאֵ֔לֶּה יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ מוֹרִ֥ישׁ אוֹתָ֖ם מִפָּנֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: You must be blameless before the LORD your God.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD your God.
You must live with God.
You must be blameless before God.
You must not do evil things.
You must not follow the ways of other nations.
You must obey God completely.
passages.original: תָּמִ֣ים תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה עִ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃ס

passages.text: Though these nations, which you will dispossess, listen to conjurers and diviners, the LORD your God has not permitted you to do so.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
You will take the land from certain nations.
These nations listen to conjurers.
These nations listen to diviners.
The LORD your God does not allow you to do this.
You must not act like these nations.
passages.original: כִּ֣י׀ הַגּוֹיִ֣ם הָאֵ֗לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֤ר אַתָּה֙ יוֹרֵ֣שׁ אוֹתָ֔ם אֶל־ מְעֹנְנִ֥ים וְאֶל־ קֹסְמִ֖ים יִשְׁמָ֑עוּ וְאַתָּ֕ה לֹ֣א כֵ֔ן נָ֛תַן לְךָ֖ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers. You must listen to him.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
The LORD will choose a prophet for you.
This prophet will be like me, Moses.
He will come from among your own people.
You must listen to this prophet.
passages.original: נָבִ֨יא מִקִּרְבְּךָ֤ מֵאַחֶ֙יךָ֙ כָּמֹ֔נִי יָקִ֥ים לְךָ֖ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ אֵלָ֖יו תִּשְׁמָעֽוּן׃

passages.text: This is what you asked of the LORD your God at Horeb on the day of the assembly, when you said, “Let us not hear the voice of the LORD our God or see this great fire anymore, so that we will not die!”
passages.sermon:
The Israelites gathered at Horeb.
This was the day of the assembly.
You spoke to the LORD your God.
You made a request to Him.
You said, “We do not want to hear the voice of the LORD our God again.
We do not want to see this great fire anymore.
We are afraid we will die.”
passages.original: כְּכֹ֨ל אֲשֶׁר־ שָׁאַ֜לְתָּ מֵעִ֨ם יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ בְּחֹרֵ֔ב בְּי֥וֹם הַקָּהָ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹ֣א אֹסֵ֗ף לִשְׁמֹ֙עַ֙ אֶת־ קוֹל֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֔י וְאֶת־ הָאֵ֨שׁ הַגְּדֹלָ֥ה הַזֹּ֛את לֹֽא־ אֶרְאֶ֥ה ע֖וֹד וְלֹ֥א אָמֽוּת׃

passages.text: Then the LORD said to me, “They have spoken well.
passages.sermon: The LORD spoke to me.\r\nThe LORD said, “They have spoken well.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י הֵיטִ֖יבוּ אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֵּֽרוּ׃

passages.text: I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their brothers. I will put My words in his mouth, and he will tell them everything I command him.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God promised to raise up a prophet for the people.
This prophet will come from among their own brothers.
This prophet will be like Moses.
God will put His words in the prophet’s mouth.
The prophet will speak everything God commands him.
The prophet will tell the people all that God says.
passages.original: נָבִ֨יא אָקִ֥ים לָהֶ֛ם מִקֶּ֥רֶב אֲחֵיהֶ֖ם כָּמ֑וֹךָ וְנָתַתִּ֤י דְבָרַי֙ בְּפִ֔יו וְדִבֶּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אֵ֖ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲצַוֶּֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: And I will hold accountable anyone who does not listen to My words that the prophet speaks in My name.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Moses.
God promises to send a prophet like Moses.
This prophet will come from among the Israelites.
God will put His words in the prophet’s mouth.
The prophet will speak everything God commands.
Anyone who does not listen to God’s words spoken by the prophet will be held accountable by God.
God Himself will require an answer from that person.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֗ה הָאִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־ יִשְׁמַע֙ אֶל־ דְּבָרַ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְדַבֵּ֖ר בִּשְׁמִ֑י אָנֹכִ֖י אֶדְרֹ֥שׁ מֵעִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But if any prophet dares to speak a message in My name that I have not commanded him to speak, or to speak in the name of other gods, that prophet must be put to death.”
passages.sermon:
A prophet is a person who claims to speak for God.
If a prophet dares to speak a message in God's name that God did not command, that prophet acts wrongly.
If a prophet speaks in the name of other gods, that prophet acts wrongly.
God commands that such a prophet must be put to death.
passages.original: אַ֣ךְ הַנָּבִ֡יא אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָזִיד֩ לְדַבֵּ֨ר דָּבָ֜ר בִּשְׁמִ֗י אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־ צִוִּיתִיו֙ לְדַבֵּ֔ר וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר יְדַבֵּ֔ר בְּשֵׁ֖ם אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וּמֵ֖ת הַנָּבִ֥יא הַהֽוּא׃

passages.text: You may ask in your heart, “How can we recognize a message that the LORD has not spoken?”
passages.sermon: The people may have a question in their hearts.\r\nThey may wonder about God's messages.\r\nThey may ask, “How can we know if a message did not come from the LORD?”
passages.original: וְכִ֥י תֹאמַ֖ר בִּלְבָבֶ֑ךָ אֵיכָה֙ נֵדַ֣ע אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־ דִבְּר֖וֹ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: When a prophet speaks in the name of the LORD and the message does not come to pass or come true, that is a message the LORD has not spoken. The prophet has spoken presumptuously. Do not be afraid of him.
passages.sermon:
A prophet is a person who claims to speak in the name of the LORD.
If a prophet speaks a message in the name of the LORD, and the message does not happen, that message is false.
The LORD did not speak that message.
The prophet has spoken with pride and presumption.
Do not be afraid of that prophet.
passages.original: אֲשֶׁר֩ יְדַבֵּ֨ר הַנָּבִ֜יא בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֗ה וְלֹֽא־ יִהְיֶ֤ה הַדָּבָר֙ וְלֹ֣א יָב֔וֹא ה֣וּא הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־ דִבְּר֖וֹ יְהוָ֑ה בְּזָדוֹן֙ דִּבְּר֣וֹ הַנָּבִ֔יא לֹ֥א תָג֖וּר מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃ס
